status.status: US allows H200 under case-by-case licenses with a 25% cut, but Beijing still withholds approval for large-scale imports: ~600,000 H200s sit in Hong Kong, and several major Chinese internet firms have each received only ~10,000.

Trump announced on Dec 8, 2025 that H200 exports to approved Chinese customers would be allowed with a 25% fee; BIS moved H200/MI325X license reviews to case-by-case (rule issued Jan 13, effective Jan 15, 2026) subject to security requirements.
status.source: U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security

status.status: NVIDIA took a $0.4B H200 excess-inventory charge in H1 FY27; licensed H200 shipments were <1% of Data Center revenue, must pass US inspection and carry a 25% US import tariff, and NVIDIA assumes no China data-center compute revenue in guidance.
April 2025 license requirement on H20 led to a $4.5B charge; licenses granted August 2025 yielded only ~$60M of H20 revenue, with US officials expecting 15%+ of licensed revenue (never codified).
The Cyberspace Administration of China summoned Nvidia on July 31, 2025 to explain alleged H20 backdoor/security risks, shortly after the US signalled H20 sales could resume.

status.topic: CAC order to stop buying Nvidia RTX Pro 6000D
status.status: China's Cyberspace Administration told ByteDance, Alibaba and other tech firms to stop testing and ordering Nvidia's China-specific RTX Pro 6000D (first reported by the FT).
Regulators in Beijing strongly discouraged Alibaba, ByteDance and others from buying Nvidia's H20, though firms remained keen and sought reassurance on orders.

status.topic: Chinese customs crackdown on Nvidia imports
status.status: From October 2025 Chinese customs teams at major ports stepped up inspections of Nvidia data-center chips, focused on H20 and RTX 6000D, coordinated with the CAC.

Rescinded by BIS on May 13, 2025 with a promise of a replacement rule; as of June 2026 no replacement had been issued, and GAO ruled (May 12, 2026) that the non-enforcement announcement was itself a 'rule' under the Congressional Review Act.
Suspension extended again to January 10, 2027 (was due to lapse Nov 2026), in line with the extended US-China trade truce.

Proclamation signed Jan 14, 2026 imposes an immediate 25% tariff on a narrow set of advanced computing chips (e.g., H200, MI325X), with exemptions for chips used in US data centers, R&D and other domestic uses; broader phase depends on negotiations.
The GAIN AI Act (US-customer right of first refusal on AI chips) passed the Senate as part of the FY2026 NDAA but the House version lacked it and it lost steam in final NDAA negotiations.
House Foreign Affairs Committee advanced the Chip Security Act (anti-smuggling / location-verification for exported AI chips) on March 26, 2026; full House passage not verified.

The one-year Busan truce of Oct 2025 was formally extended on Nov 9, 2026 to January 10, 2027: tariff reductions kept, China suspends critical-mineral export controls and its 24% tariff on US goods for two months.

status.topic: China gallium/germanium/antimony export ban to US
status.status: MOFCOM suspended its Dec 2024 ban on exports of gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials to the US until November 27, 2026; no extension verified as of this file's date.
